question.problem:
Given that the function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193886/assets/f72fd02a0488c44ac7472487222507c5739853cd25720502a726844e0c23c915.svg)
is continuous at $x=0,$ find the value of the constant $b.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=0,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}\sqrt{2b-3x} \\  & =\sqrt{2b-3(0)} \\  & =\sqrt{2b},\end{aligned}
$$

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}(-x+2) \\  & =-(0)+2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=0,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) \\ 2 & =\sqrt{2b} \\ 4 & =2b \\ b & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
